effort: Revisit the original ankle-spring marker, apply controlled stance-force tasks and establish an honest end-of-curriculum gym record.
brief: E1 repeats the original marker under its original conditions before fatigue. Three new low-dose receiving constraints examine shared-to-split, lateral single-leg push to shared receiving and force from a paused single-leg start. Two familiar planted-foot hip-drive tasks close the explosive work without more landings. Familiar light control and six one-round strength roles support interpretation without manufacturing a final workload peak.
marker: Repeat Class 1's two sets of eight stationary bilateral ankle pogos: hands on hips, low height, soft knees, same surface/shoes where recorded, 60 s after each set. Count clean centred landings with stable rhythm and no progressive deep knee bend/trunk drift. Compare with Class 1 only if actual compatible observations exist; otherwise record a new baseline and compare the two current sets only.
review: Class 11 prescribed no flight, 46 brief rapid-force efforts and six primary rounds; actual response is unknown. The full saved sequence and initial Class 1 anchor were reviewed. Class 12 deliberately repeats three explosive defaults for anchor/skill continuity while adding three small related receiving variants. Primary work stays at six rounds rather than automatically restoring the initial nine-round workload.
sequence: E1 is unchanged from the initial marker and stays first. E2–E4 have only two attempts per stated stance/side and full resets. E5/E6 deliberately return known hip-force tasks with feet planted; they are not presented as unique new drills.

E.name: Stationary Bilateral Ankle Pogo
E.job: Repeat the original ankle-spring marker under matched conditions to distinguish a real recorded change from a different task.
E.cue: Hands on hips, small centred two-foot bounces, knees soft and ankles free. Record clean contacts within each set; stop for drift, progressive knee bend or rhythm loss. Lower amplitude for control and label changed conditions rather than forcing a comparison.

E.name: Two-Foot Forward Jump to Split-Stance Stick
E.job: Receive a small shared forward push in a controlled split base, assigning a clear lead/trail support role.
E.cue: Parallel two-foot start, modest forward jump, place feet in a short split stance together and hold 2 s with pelvis forward. No long split, twist or second jump. Shorten distance/stance if front knee or rear ankle alignment is lost.

E.name: Single-Leg Lateral Jump to Two-Foot Landing
E.family: unilateral frontal push with shared receiving
E.job: Express a short lateral stance-leg push while both legs share the receiving load.
E.cue: Start on one foot, push a small distance outward, land on both feet parallel beneath the body and hold 2 s. Face forward with no crossover or turn. Reduce distance for reaching or trunk lean.

E.name: Paused Single-Leg Squat Jump to Two-Foot Landing
E.job: Produce a controlled one-leg push from a still partial squat, separating force initiation from countermovement assistance.
E.cue: Hold a small single-leg knee/hip bend for 2 s, push quickly to a modest height without another dip, receive on both feet and hold 2 s. Use a shallower start for control; no maximum-height target. An unstable pause is a fault, not a reason for extra attempts.

E.name: Split-Stance Medicine Ball Forward Scoop Toss
E.family: asymmetric hip drive with pelvic control
E.job: Retain a familiar split-base forward hip-force expression after the receiving tasks, without another landing demand.
E.cue: Use Class 6's short split stance and light ball; shallow dip and fast forward scoop with both feet planted and pelvis facing ahead. No rotation, catch or step. Reduce load for an arm-only heave/back arch; retrieve by walking after the ball stops.

E.name: Two-Hand Kettlebell Swing
E.job: Revisit the original planted-foot ballistic hip-drive skill with a familiar complete swing cycle.
E.cue: Two hands, stable parallel feet, light-to-moderate bell chosen for crisp speed. Hinge and snap tall; bell floats no higher than chest, no arm lifting/back arch. Park after five. Use actual prior load only if recorded and appropriate; it is not a mandated increase.

S.name: Short-Foot Drill
S.job: Retain the original light arch-control role for a stable contact and lifting platform.
S.cue: Both feet supported, target one arch at a time, long toes and heel grounded. Relax fully between holds. Use seated execution instead for cramping or toe gripping; do not increase effort to make the final class harder.

S.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
S.job: Retain the original low-fatigue hip-abductor support role for pelvic control.
S.cue: Pelvis stacked, bottom knee bent, top leg straight and slightly behind trunk; lift 2 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce range for rolling or hip hike; bodyweight only and at least five clean reps available.

P.name: Split Squat — two dumbbells at sides
P.cue: Floor split stance, front foot planted, pelvis square; lower 2 s and rise firmly for 1 s. Reduce load/range for collapse or balance loss. Use one DB with stable hand support instead of two unsupported DBs if needed; counts stay the same.
P.job: Record a familiar challenging stance-force set on each leg under the original exercise geometry.
P.decision: Original Class 1 2 × 6 per leg → final 1 × 6 per leg, retaining Class 11's smaller working allocation. Compare first-set load/quality only if actual prior geometry/effort records exist; different preceding workloads limit interpretation.

P.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
P.cue: Soft knees, hips back, DBs close; lower 3 s and rise in 1 s. Stop the descent before back rounding; reduce load/range if the hinge becomes spinal movement.
P.job: Record a familiar controlled hip-hinge strength set without a final volume peak.
P.decision: Original 2 × 6 → final 1 × 6; keep the established tempo and actual suitable range. This is consolidation, not an earned heavier load.

P.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated dumbbells
P.cue: Both legs together, knees near 90°, heels start on floor, hands secure DBs on lower thighs above knees. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce load for bounce/lost heel height. If bench fit is unsuitable, use supported standing bent-knee calf raises instead, same reps/rest, and log changed knee angle.
P.job: Record knee-flexed ankle force with the original seated angle/heel range where actual setup is known.
P.decision: Original 2 × 8 → final 1 × 8. Compare compatible first-set execution/load cautiously; no extra set or weight is required to claim completion.

P.name: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise — supported single leg
P.cue: Work from floor, near-straight soft knee, one DB and stable hand support. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce load or use bodyweight for lost range; use 1 × 8 bilateral instead of per-leg work if even unilateral bodyweight is too demanding, with 1 × 4 bilateral preparation.
P.job: Retain the original one-set straight-knee ankle-force role on each leg.

P.name: Glute Bridge Walkout
P.cue: Keep a floor bridge while four small alternating heel steps go out and four return; eight steps at about 1 s each = one full cycle. Choose reach so four cycles are challenging with 2–3 whole cycles available. Shorten reach for pelvic sag or cramping; do not add steps or cycles.
P.job: Return to the original controlled knee-flexor cycle task using a recorded lever only if available.
P.decision: Four-cycle role returns after Class 11's floor bridge. Log heel reach/partial cycles; do not equate bridge reps with walkout cycles or infer tolerance.

P.name: Supine Band-resisted Hip Flexion
P.cue: Secure loop band around both forefeet; nonworking leg straight with heel grounded. Flex working hip/knee toward thigh-vertical in 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s without arching or moving the anchor heel. Reduce tension/range for pelvic tilt. If a secure loop is unavailable, use seated DB hip flexion instead with hands securing the DB above the knee: same dose/rest, small controlled thigh lift; preparation unloaded.
P.job: Retain the original resisted leg-recovery role with a controlled pelvis.

equipment: E1 requires the original surface/hand/footwear conditions only for a true comparison; if those are unavailable, record changed conditions. E2 may use a parallel two-foot landing instead when split receiving is unsuitable, same four events/rest. E4 may use a light rear-toe kickstand paused takeoff instead when a single-leg pause cannot be controlled, same 1 × 2 per lead side and two-foot receiving; record the altered takeoff. E5 without safe contained throwing space uses Class 11's split-stance held-ball hip drive instead, same six total force efforts, no throws. E6 without competent swing/handling uses a light fast floor hip bridge instead, 2 × 5 with 90 s rest and a 2 s lowering phase, replacing ten swings with ten nonflight hip drives. Do not add a comparison test outside these rows.
count_note: E1 sixteen + E2 four + E3 four + E4 four = 28 two-foot landing events, 56 individual foot contacts. E3/E4 have unilateral takeoff but bilateral receiving; no single-leg landing is prescribed. E5 adds six throws and E6 ten swings. Primary work stays at six rounds; initial two-set strength doses are not automatically restored. Comparable records require actual observations and matching exercise conditions, not merely the same exercise name.
novelty: Three deliberate explosive repeat exceptions close the sequence: E1 repeats Class 1 for the only exact initial pogo comparison; E5 repeats Class 6 for familiar asymmetrical hip-force skill; E6 repeats Class 1 for familiar swing execution. E2–E4 add small force-sharing/start-condition variants with clear jobs. This honors the push for drill variety without presenting a renamed test or unnecessary complex novelty as a better final comparison. Light and primary strength recur intentionally.
audit: Preserved the original E1 dose/position/rest before fatigue; did not claim that different jump variants measure improvement. Rejected a maximal jump/strength test and an automatic return to nine primary rounds. Three new receiving/start variants use small fully reset doses, while the familiar no-flight tasks limit impact. All twelve classes must still pass the full-sequence audit before the written curriculum is declared complete.
progression: If actual Class 1 and Class 12 records are compatible, describe observed differences without attributing all change to this curriculum. If prior observations are absent, leave improvement unknown and use today's record as a baseline. Future support work should maintain, advance one justified variable, or regress from actual execution and recovery; no Class 13 or new running block is prescribed here.
map_note: Original pogo comparison plus purposeful repeat exceptions; six primary rounds, no final workload peak.
next_job: Full-sequence audit, then await actual athlete feedback for implementation or revision.
handoff: Audit all twelve saved classes for exact framework/6–2–6 counts, meaningful variety, conditional progression, workload, recovery, timing, source/library accuracy and saved-state integrity. Correct substantive inconsistencies, save the completed curriculum and handoff, then stop; actual athlete completion remains unknown.

final_review: Reviewed the final class against the initial marker and current request. Three explosive defaults deliberately recur, while three receiving/start variants have specific jobs. E1 matches the original first-position pogo dose/rest; strength remains at six rounds with no invented improvement or final workload peak. Twenty-eight two-foot landings and separate throws/swings are consistent. Proceeding to the required full-sequence audit before declaring completion.
